findings.title: Late BIP38 completion restores cleared secret results
findings.reproduction: Execute the actual installer with a memory DOM and deferred synthetic decryptor. Start decrypt, Clear, then resolve; repeat with a replacement run started before the old result resolves.
findings.expected: Clear revokes publication by the old operation. Old completion cannot create secret inputs, enable reveal or mutate a new password/status/progress state.
findings.observed: After Clear the old completion retains two secret inputs and enables reveal while the result container stays hidden. After Clear plus a new run the old inputs are in the visible results and the replacement password is cleared.
findings.impact: A supported secret-lifetime operation is undone by pending work. Evidence is local DOM retention and cross-run mutation, not egress, unauthorized spending or proof of heap erasure failure.
findings.recommendedFix: Give the local BIP38 secret session an operation token. Check it after every await before success/error DOM writes and before password/reveal/progress finalization. Dispose stale mutable outputs; keep cryptographic values local.
findings.requiredVerification: Deferred success and rejection after Clear, old completion during a replacement run and idempotent disposal, using synthetic data without scrypt; then the nearest small Inspector lifecycle tests.

evidence.method: Coordinator-executed focused probe; independent reviewer checked evidence, not a second execution

result.executionScope: Actual installer with injected memory DOM/deferred synthetic decryptor; no browser, clipboard or real KDF

evidence.limitations: No browser, clipboard, real KDF or real wallet material. Rejection path was read but not separately executed.

findings.releaseBlockingReason: Restore the supported Clear/secret publication guarantee before releasing this affected feature; medium reflects bounded demonstrated local impact.

findings.title: Verification-record inventory reads a nested MHFE directory as a file
findings.reproduction: Execute exact generatedDirectories and wasm declarations from create-verification-record.mjs with real read-only fs on the current package tree, without running the entry point.
findings.expected: Supported record generation enumerates all included nested package files deterministically, using the same admitted manifest as provenance.
findings.observed: The enumeration fragment exits 1 with EISDIR for packages/recovery-mhfe-wasm/generated/core. It enumerates one level and attempts readFileSync on each entry.
findings.impact: The mandatory package inventory step cannot construct the current nested MHFE records. Full prerequisite checks and release entry point were not run; this is not a completed release failure or a secret-compromise claim.
findings.recommendedFix: Implement the VendoredMhfePackage extraction below. Include modules.json, nested core/runtime/repair/passwords/wallet files and both Argon2 engines; retain the documented helper exclusion. Do not merely skip directories.
findings.requiredVerification: Deterministic nested manifest fixture with exact expected paths and hashes, missing/extra/unsafe entries and both engines. Exercise supported record generation once prerequisites are met; full release procedure only when requested.

findings.title: Child-wallet totals above fifty bypass bounded derivation batches
findings.reproduction: Run the actual extracted child-wallet derivation function with host/UI stubs at count 51 and a fake worker using real assertBatch. Compare the real shared streamed function for the same total.
findings.expected: The advertised total range through 200 is split into per-worker batches no greater than 50, preserving order, revisions and atomic child publication.
findings.observed: The shared stream submits [50,1]. The child flow submits [51] and fails: Error: Number of results must be an integer from 1 to 50.
findings.impact: A supported child-wallet result count fails for adapters using the common bound. No wrong keys, partial private reveal or universal adapter failure was established.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the existing bounded stream with a child-owned atomic accumulator and failure cleanup. Keep the 200-total UI policy distinct from the 50-per-worker cap.
findings.requiredVerification: Count 50/51/200 with synthetic worker results, final-index limits, failure in a later chunk and input-revision/cancellation checks; nearest public child-wallet known answer.

findings.title: BIP85 public API accepts unsupported mnemonic word counts
findings.reproduction: Bundle the current public API in memory. Confirm the existing published 12-word known answer, then call with runtime words=13 and index 0 using the public test root.
findings.expected: The advertised 12/15/18/21/24 contract rejects unsupported runtime counts before entropy derivation; a TypeScript union is not a runtime check.
findings.observed: The 12-word answer matches. words=13 is accepted and returns 17 bytes at m/83696968'/39'/0'/13'/0'. Subsequent BIP39 conversion refuses that entropy length.
findings.impact: Malformed output escapes the public API. Normal HTML selections are supported and downstream conversion refuses; no ordinary valid-selection key fault or secret compromise was shown.
findings.recommendedFix: Call shared mnemonic count validation/width lookup before entropyAt. Keep the public boundary check and derive output width from its owner.
findings.requiredVerification: Direct JS unsupported counts, fractions/unsafe values and existing five supported-count known/refusal cases. Expected values remain independent of the new parameter implementation.

evidence.method: Coordinator-executed focused probe; independent reviewer checked evidence, not a second execution
evidence.limitations: Actual public core API and exact existing known answer; HTML path not executed.

findings.title: Chosen-word invalidation depends on an optional MHFE feature
findings.reproduction: Trace a base chosen-word composition that excludes recovery-mhfe. While generation has yielded, edit wishes. Compare base wish handlers and controller revision with optional checked installer handlers.
findings.expected: Base chosen-word generation owns change/cancel notification independently of optional checked generation, so an edited request cannot publish an old-wish result.
findings.observed: Base handlers update diagnostics without aborting or incrementing the controller revision. The optional checked installer provides the invalidation hook in the default composition. Without it, the captured old wish result can still pass the unchanged revision guard.
findings.impact: The optional-feature composition has stale intent behavior. This is a precise static trace; no browser or complete event-order reproduction and no entropy reduction were demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Make the base ChosenWords feature own wish-change notification; controller and checked mode subscribe by composition. Preserve passphrase intent and final source/wish readback.
findings.requiredVerification: Small event-order regression for edit during a yielded generation, MHFE included/excluded and checked mode on/off; optional graph must remain pruned.

findings.title: MnemoCode job notifications are not all qualified by input revision
findings.reproduction: Read worker-job control flow after capturing the input revision; compare success, progress and non-cancellation error handling while inputs change.
findings.expected: Current job/input identity qualifies progress, errors and final status as well as the successful result.
findings.observed: Successful stale outcomes are rejected and wiped. Progress updates status without that revision check; non-cancellation errors are rethrown without qualification at this seam.
findings.impact: Stale progress/error feedback may describe edited inputs. No stale secret publication or overlapping-run reachability was demonstrated; caller policies can narrow impact.
findings.recommendedFix: Use a local job/input token for notifications and completion. Keep confirmation, cancellation semantics and stale-outcome wiping; do not invent one superclass for all utility jobs.
findings.requiredVerification: Synthetic deferred progress/error after input edits and cancellation; successful stale-result wipe must remain. No PDF rendering or heavy recovery replay is needed.

findings.title: Public export completion is not consistently bound to its result snapshot
findings.reproduction: Compare Activity workbook publication after await, external Activity exportState identity handling and Scanner broker reply after staged exports are cleared.
findings.expected: Export success/error/status uses the snapshot that initiated it and cannot mutate a replacement result's controls. Each host explicitly defines stale download semantics.
findings.observed: Dash Activity publishes/downloads after an unqualified workbook await. External Activity gates success by identity but not rejection. Scanner can publish late broker status after Clear removed staged exports.
findings.impact: Bounded stale public feedback or export timing. Scanner request was explicitly authorized; no demonstrated promise that Clear revokes an issued download, private-key export or egress defect.
findings.recommendedFix: Qualify notifications/publication by local result identity. Decide stale download behavior explicitly. If Scanner needs cancellation, use attributed request IDs in the trusted shell while preserving opaque vault and fixed public projections.
findings.requiredVerification: Synthetic delayed serializers/broker replies for Clear, replacement and rejection; retain workbook string/cell and public-envelope assertions without generating many PDFs.

findings.title: Wallet parameter and cryptographic preparation rules have multiple owners
findings.reproduction: Inspect the challenged definition register and compare the cited complete rule/mechanism implementations. This is a source ownership finding, not an executed cryptographic or build divergence claim.
findings.expected: Every rule/mechanism has one appropriate owner and front ends delegate, as required by the workspace OOP/DRY instructions; callers and independent oracles are not duplicates.
findings.observed: 13 coherent families retain multiple scoped owners. Their per-facet counts, exact locations and proposed modules are listed below; facets are not summed as copies.
findings.impact: Maintenance violates explicit one-owner rules and increases the chance of later drift. Most cited owners currently agree. Separate behavior defects are tracked under their own IDs; similar source is not proof of cryptographic weakness.
findings.recommendedFix: Perform the listed family migrations using existing helpers first, small data/assessment owners and composition. Keep public/private realms, optional graphs, protocol contexts and independent refusal/known-answer expectations separate.
findings.requiredVerification: Use each family's focused regression contract, then the small module-boundary/composition checks. Add delegation/owner assertions only where they establish the semantic rule; no full vector replay on routine refactors.

findings.title: Build-profile tests assert inactive entry metadata
findings.reproduction: Compare six UI and two worker metadata fields in build-profile-definitions with the actual generated stdin entry factories and current profile tests.
findings.expected: Profile metadata and its tests describe fields the active builders consume, or clearly label reference-only values.
findings.observed: Eight inspected fields are inactive in the current Deriver/Viewer/Scanner generated-entry paths; tests still assert their strings. Inspector's entryPoint is live.
findings.impact: Tests can stay green without proving the active entry composition. This is not proof that the named source modules themselves are dead.
findings.recommendedFix: Remove or explicitly label inactive fields and test actual entry factories/dispatch. Preserve Inspector's live entry and meaningful independent composition expectations.
findings.requiredVerification: Small generated-entry and profile tests plus existing composition/boundary tests; no exhaustive matrix rebuild needed for the metadata-only correction.

findings.title: Security audit overview identifies an older report as latest
findings.reproduction: Read SECURITY_AUDIT.md:7 and the retained local chronological index before this new audit is appended.
findings.expected: An overview links to the current audit index without presenting an older source review as the latest assessment.
findings.observed: The overview calls AUD-020 latest while the dirty checkout already contains retained AUD-021/022/023. A focused AUD-018 reference is also not the current full overview.
findings.impact: A reader can mistake older coverage/status for current evidence. This describes the local checkout; remote publication state was not checked.
findings.recommendedFix: Prefer a stable link to the chronological audit index and snapshot-specific verification record. No broad AuditCatalog class is needed for one stale sentence.
findings.requiredVerification: Read the rendered link targets and run the repository's short documentation/project-fact checks when making the correction.

families.classification: Concrete rule/mechanism ownership duplication; no severity inferred from number of sites

duplicationRegister.excluded: Calls/delegating wrappers; type unions; singly defined lists; independent expected vectors/refusals; vendor/generated copies; distinct normalization/consensus/CSP/realm policies; missing checks and stale docs; prior AUD-023-ARC002
duplicationRegister.countReconciliation: All40 initial candidates challenged; overlaps merged and parameter roles split. MnemoCode job counters, Inspector/public-export revisions and Scanner run shape excluded as semantic clone families; concrete bugs remain separately recorded.

roadmap.work: Restore concrete supported behavior before broad moves
roadmap.reason: BIP38 publication and nested MHFE records are release blockers for their affected features. Use the existing stream/count owners and local operation checks. Add the specific bounded regressions, without making a broad refactor a prerequisite.
Read-only parameter leaves remove UI copies with small impact. Preserve user-intent checks and final public-boundary calls; base chosen words must remain independent of optional MHFE.

roadmap.work: Move protocol data and codecs to appropriate public-safe leaves
roadmap.reason: Keep private derivation imports out of online data services and Bitcoin/Ethereum text out of Dash-only graphs. Each consumer retains its admission/reveal policy.

roadmap.work: Consolidate exact data interpretation and resource lifetimes
roadmap.reason: Use small value/lifetime owners and private calculations by composition. Keep consensus contexts, default budgets, failure/progress strategies and trusted download authority explicit.

Reuse existing manifests and helpers. Share assembly mechanics, not CSP policies. Preserve both MHFE Argon2 modes, launchers and Envelope's Argon2. Release byte comparison remains separately authorized, not routine refactor work.

optionalOpportunities: A private bounded-safe-integer helper may reduce similar predicates, but caller bounds/labels/end-range meanings stay explicit. Four generic-looking predicates are not four copies of one protocol rule.

Scanner candidate/seed/watch runs can compose a small control-state helper only if useful. Their current UI blocks Clear/new-start while running; fail-fast and per-coin error policies differ. No generic scan superclass or new lifecycle defect is inferred from shape alone.

Scanner builder uses a closing-tag replacement literal with a JS identity escape; source intent warrants a focused final-assembly fixture. Actual exploitability and default bundler escaping were not tested, so this is not a vulnerability finding.

Use delegation/parameter-source tests for selected high-risk owners and independent negative/known-answer fixtures. Equality tests alone can keep two identical copies green; token-count tests and importing production helpers into expected-output oracles are insufficient.

Long functions/classes are reading cues, not defects by size. Do not create one-method classes for pure conversions, a global RuleCatalog or one JobSession superclass across private/public/vault realms.

Workspace guidance still names Rust 1.98.1 while current builders/container pins say 1.99.0. Reconcile authoritative guidance when updating it; no toolchain or global settings were changed during this audit.

historicalFollowup.currentSource: MnemoCodeShares delegates many policies but still owns restore orchestration. No second upstream implementation was counted in this review.
historicalFollowup.handoff: Upstream MnemoCode session must supply the host-neutral ShareRestore before authorized sync/delegation; no message or upstream edit was required by this review-only task.

limitations: This is a source-wide architecture/DRY review with bounded focused behavior probes, not an independent security certification or proof that every body/rule has been examined.

558 owned TS/MJS/Rust files and 81,273 lines inventoried; generated/vendor internals, tests/oracles, wordlists and synced upstream MnemoCode source are not counted as first-party duplicate implementations. Scope inventory is not manual line-by-line coverage.

1,851 qualifying function bodies out of 4,993 AST function nodes, threshold 35 nodes and 6 lines. Identifier-renaming candidates are not binding-aware. Rust has no AST clone detection in this harness.

The resolved 1,784-edge static first-party graph has no detected runtime SCC or unresolved scoped imports; it is not a complete generated/virtual/worker/dynamic/external graph or a trust-boundary proof.
All 34 families are an inspected lower bound with separate per-facet counts, not a repository-total duplicate count. Definition facets overlap; no global extra-copy number is computed.

No browsers, full vector replays, full-size KDFs, mass PDF/card rendering, release matrix, Docker/native/WASM rebuild, live provider requests, installations, remote CI, commits, pushes, tags or releases.
Real MHFE/MnemoCode native/browser parity and upstream internals were not freshly reviewed. Existing deferred ShareRestore extraction keeps original AUD-023-ARC002 identity.

Five final focused probes reach expected open contract failures, exit 1. AST/host stubs have narrower scope than entry point/browser/real crypto execution. Four original harness compatibility/fixture errors are separately retained.

Node heap capped at 1,536 MiB and Vitest at one worker; no heavy run launched. Memory snapshots were below 14 GiB system use, but a global continuous peak/RSS limit across unrelated sessions was not enforced.
Model/effort exact client metadata is unavailable and left null; no retrospective model-setting inference.
assessment: Six medium and eight low new findings. Two supported behavior/inventory blockers before release. No new proof of direct key compromise, normal supported derivation error, network egress, or unsafe entropy distribution. Source rule ownership is not compliant despite passing bounded boundary/composition tests.
changeScope: Audit reports, index and rerunnable audit harnesses only; product code and both repository source snapshots unchanged. No findings fixed, no commits or releases.

evidence.commandLogIntegrity: Each command record contains exact command, UTC interval, exit code and logSha256; local SHA256SUMS is a supplemental manifest.

executiveSummary.result: 34 coherent duplication families, 144 distinct inspected source locations; six medium and eight low new findings. Five behavior defects reproduced, one additional medium defect traced statically.
